rows.en: Impossible. An ending like this is impossible!
Do you want to die, rookie?

rows.notes: Whisper wrote a nonsense word (hyukku); read as hiyokko (rookie), matching the neighbouring partner-scold lines.

rows.en: I'll thank you for the help.
I'd have been fine on my own.
Guess there was no need for me to sortie.
Guess I enjoyed the dance a bit too much.
Damn it, we didn't make it in time.
Failure? I won't accept it. I won't!
Me, failing? That's a joke that isn't funny.
Give covering fire. Don't waste ammo.
Fall back and cover my rear.
I'll draw the enemy in. Cover me.
Move up and act as a decoy!
I'm leaving the melee to you.

rows.notes: Whisper wrote an extra syllable (yokoo); read as sagatteroyo.

rows.en: Attacking isn't all there is to fighting!
Stay quiet until your next orders.
I'll show you how to really fight.
I need you to get it together, Captain.
I'm taking command from here. Let's go.
A rookie for a captain? Spare me.
What is this song? I'm pulling out.
There's no way to fight in this situation.
To think a song would move even me.
Don't hog all the fun, Captain.

rows.notes: Whisper wrote gookingudana; guessed sasuga da na (well done) before the partner's name Nora.

rows.en: Flying shoulder to shoulder with a rookie. A nice little stroll, huh.
Tch, got stuck with a worthless partner.
rows.notes: Whisper wrote kumasarete; read as kumasarete (was paired with).

rows.en: Listen. Just don't get in my way.
Let's see what you can do.
Mission's starting. Can you do it?

rows.notes: Whisper wrote yokko; read as hiyokko (rookie).

rows.en: I'm expecting good work from you.
Looks like I can have fun with you.
Don't go stealing my kills, too.
rows.notes: Whisper wrote tamashii (soul); read as emono (prey/kill) to match the partner-lines of this block. Literal reading would be 'don't take even my soul'.
Whisper wrote shinuguri; read as omori (babysitting), as in Roy's matching clip.

rows.en: What do you think a battlefield is?
Looks like the mission's a success. Returning.
How many times do I have to say it? Handle your machine like a lady, delicate as a feather.
rows.notes: Whisper wrote 'shojo' (many women); read as shukujo (lady).

rows.en: I expect you to handle at least this much.
You handle your machine boldly, but it's not bad.
You've grown into quite a man.
rows.notes: Whisper wrote yoko (side); read as otoko (man) or ude (arm/skill). Block 300-331 is for a male partner; Nora's matching clip says 'man's face'.

rows.en: Just what I'd expect from a pilot I acknowledge.
